the title seems kinda confusing, the main distinction seems to be this is using nix-instantiate rather than nix-env, right?

Also, the entry point `packages-info.nix` handles the logic done by nix-env in nix code, leading to us being able to do changes to the interface without needing to break usages of nix-env.

To be honest, the best case would be if we used the packages.json generated by Hydra and didn't need to handle the implementation of how to generate the metadata here.

e.g., take it from `https://channels.nixos.org/${channel}/packages.json.br` which would be `https://channels.nixos.org/nixos-unstable/packages.json.br` for unstable.

I can see several advantages of using `https://channels.nixos.org/${channel}/packages.json.br`:

* performance: no need to do that work again
* consistency across tools, if they all use that set
* having one implementation of putting together that set makes it potentially easier to evolve

However, I also see disadvantages:

* we can no longer run flake-info against a version of nixpkgs that is _not_ a channel, e.g. testing changes on a branch
* what if we'd _want_ to index more than is published there? are we sure it's the same set today?

One option might be to carry both implementations so you can pick...not sure that's worth it though. WDYT?
we could go happy path until we know we got a clear use-case to carry both?

> we could go happy path until we know we got a clear use-case to carry both?

The use-case is: "I see package X is not indexed correctly. I suspect a change in nixpkgs would fix it. I have made that change on a branch. Now I want to see whether that indeed fixes it.".

Perhaps rather than supporting both different approaches, we should allow setting arbitrary URLs for this file, and document(/link to documentation for) how to generate it for your own nixpkgs branches.

> are we sure it's the same set today?

Could you validate this?

> Could you validate this?

some casual browsing of package results did not come up with anything weird for me so far, seeming in line with these being taken from the json.

issue.body:
Get package data from `packages-info.nix` instead of `packages-config.nix`.

The old approach heuristically split the derivation `name` into `pname` and `version`, which fails for packages whose `pname` contains characters that look like version separators (e.g. `sp800-90b-entropyassessment`, which [so far](https://search.nixos.org/packages?channel=25.11&include_modular_service_options=1&include_nixos_options=1&query=sp800-90b-entropyassessment) has shown as 'Name: sp800, Version: 90b-entropyassessment-1.1.8'). The new `packages-info.nix` (added in NixOS/nixpkgs#451424) reads `pname` and `version` directly from the derivation attributes, producing correct results.

Closes #770.

disclaimer i used a coding agent in the creation of this patch.
issue.title: fix(flake-info): get package versions from fetched `packages.json.br`
